scripts.//test: Runs the unit suites AND every behavioural matrix, unconditionally. This used to be `pnpm -r test && pnpm test:rls`, where one unit failure anywhere short-circuited the only tests that assert tenant isolation, and nothing recorded that they had been skipped. The matrices are now DISCOVERED from supabase/tests/*.test.mjs, so one that is added and never wired up cannot exist, and a matrix that reports no RESULT line fails the build (audit 2026-08-09).
scripts.//test:rls: The behavioural matrices alone. History worth keeping: two of them (load-lifecycle, duty-sessions) were never wired in and had not executed in months behind stale migration filenames, while the ledger quoted their pass counts — 42/42 and 20/20 — as fact. Both counts turned out to be real, but only after four unimplemented behaviours the matrices specified were actually built (migrations 0141-0143). They were also chained with `&&`, so the first failure hid the other three.
scripts.//verify:live: Answers "why don't I see my changes?" in one command: compares git HEAD + the highest migration file against the deployed API's GET /api/version. Exits non-zero on drift.
scripts.//gen:tokens: Regenerates packages/ui/src/tokens.generated.css from the DTCG sources in packages/tokens/src. The @theme inline block is DERIVED from each token's `fuelguard.expose` extension, so a role can no longer arrive without its Tailwind binding — the border-line failure mode, closed at the source rather than linted for.
scripts.//check:card-binding: Phase 2's exit gate, scripted (Step 2.6): no org may hold write_entitlement = 'confirmed' with a null probed_identity_hash. Deliberately NOT in ci.yml — it reads the live database, and this repository is public, so wiring it there would mean a production service-role key in CI secrets to check a status claim. Run it at session start and after any probe or credential change; migration 0194 enforces the same rule in Postgres.
scripts.//lint:upserts: Bans `.upsert(x, { onConflict: "id" })` into a table with NOT NULL columns the payload cannot be shown to carry. Postgres evaluates NOT NULL on the proposed tuple BEFORE conflict arbitration, so that call fails on rows that already exist — the defect that shipped three times and took the Idling and HOS syncs down (incident 2026-08-10).
scripts.//lint:tests: Fails when a *.test.* file exists that its workspace runner never collects. Third occurrence of that bug: apps/driver narrowed `include` to tests/** and 24 cases in src/ had never run (audit 2026-08-09).
scripts.//mutation:check: Breaks the code on purpose and requires the suite to go red. A SURVIVED mutation is a hole in the tests; a STALE one means the code moved and that check has been testing nothing. Runs weekly in CI (.github/workflows/mutation-check.yml).
scripts.//lint:secrets: gitleaks over `git archive HEAD` — tracked content only, so an untracked local .env never false-alarms while a committed one fails the build. Needs the gitleaks binary (brew install gitleaks).
scripts.//lint:cli-streams: efs.mjs must put ONLY a JSON result on stdout — a prompt there makes `efs.mjs <cmd> > file.json` hang, which it did on 2026-08-16.
scripts.//mcleod:inspect: Read-only reconnaissance against the carrier's LoadMaster: the 22 aggregate questions the field mapping cannot answer without measuring. Posts nothing to FuelGuard and needs no ingest token — the people best placed to run it are the carrier's IT against `lme`, before any token exists. Every query is gated by lint:mcleod-recon.
scripts.//mcleod:dry-run: Reads McLeod, maps every row, and prints per-field coverage plus one sample — without posting and without a FuelGuard ingest token. Exercises the whole carrier-side half of the integration (the SQL, the trims, the date and code handling, the change detection) against real data before the two systems are connected at all. Driver names, licences, addresses and dates of birth are masked: coverage counts prove the mapping, printing the values proves nothing extra.
scripts.//mcleod:report: The match report computed BY the pipeline, writing nothing — not a row, not even last_synced_at. This is what M3's Done-when actually asks for and the go/no-go for everything after it: its counts must reproduce the plan's hand-computed 162 / 175 / 201.
scripts.//lint:mcleod-recon: The McLeod recon pack (tools/mcleod-agent/inspect.mjs) is meant to be run by the CARRIER'S IT against `lme`, the production LoadMaster database our login cannot read (HAS_DBACCESS = 0). Its reviewer has to be able to trust 22 SQL statements without reading them closely, so the gate enforces the four properties that make it safe to hand over: every statement is a single SELECT; the outright-banned columns (social_security_no and friends — db_datareader can read it and 1,461 of 1,463 rows have one) appear nowhere at all; names, licences, addresses and contacts may be COUNTED but never returned; and anything reading driver/tractor/trailer binds @companyId, because dbo.company holds four legal entities in the same tables.
scripts.lint:codegen: node scripts/gen-rule-catalog.mjs && pnpm gen:tokens && git diff --exit-code -- 'packages/**/*.generated.ts' 'packages/ui/src/tokens.generated.css'
scripts.//lint:token-schema: The 14 role names apps/web and apps/driver genuinely share — canvas, surfaces, ink, edges. Measured 2026-08-23: of 61 web roles and 33 driver roles only those 14 overlap, so the gate pins the shared neutral ground rather than pretending the two schemas match. Everything else is the two products being different (operation-*/sync-* on driver, elevation-*/viz-*/link on web).
scripts.//lint:light-dark: Lightning CSS transpiles light-dark() into a prefers-color-scheme polyfill by default, which follows the OS and cannot be overridden by the in-app scheme toggle. Both vite configs must exclude Features.LightDark. The toggle shipped broken because every other gate reads source CSS and the rewrite happens at minification (2026-08-23).
scripts.//lint:token-gamut: Every colour token must name a colour an sRGB display can actually produce. 64 of 264 did not (2026-08-25) — ramp-caution-200 was 0.212 of linear overshoot, outside Display-P3 too. Chrome keeps oklch() all the way to PAINT rather than resolving it to rgb(), so an out-of-gamut token is mapped against the display profile: macOS colour-manages and can paint into P3, Windows does not, and the same dashboard came out visibly different on two machines driving the same monitor.
